cfg.description: SGD momentum LR 0.03 may converge more slowly than 0.1.

hypothesis: SGD momentum LR 0.03 may converge more slowly than 0.1.
mechanism: Momentum accumulates gradients; LR controls the size of each update.

cfg.description: Adam may converge faster through per-parameter adaptive updates.

hypothesis: Adam may converge faster through per-parameter adaptive updates.
mechanism: Adam uses bias-corrected first/second moments; optimizer and its LR change together for fair tuning.

cfg.description: Larger Adam LR may accelerate early fitting but increase oscillation.

hypothesis: Larger Adam LR may accelerate early fitting but increase oscillation.
mechanism: Compare each optimizer at its own best validation LR with the same 20-epoch budget.

cfg.description: MSE on raw logits versus one-hot targets may fit classification less effectively than CE.

hypothesis: MSE on raw logits versus one-hot targets may fit classification less effectively than CE.
mechanism: MSE averages (logit-one_hot)^2 over B x 7 without 1/2; it is not MSE on softmax probabilities. CE gradient is p-y; logit MSE gradient is 2*(z-y)/7. Compare F1, not loss scales.

cfg.description: Larger batch reduces updates per epoch and may slow convergence at fixed LR.

hypothesis: Larger batch reduces updates per epoch and may slow convergence at fixed LR.
mechanism: Batch 2048 changes update count, not just memory: ceil(N/2048) vs ceil(N/512) per epoch.

cfg.description: Dropout may reduce the train-val gap but hurt a baseline still improving at epoch 20.

hypothesis: Dropout may reduce the train-val gap but hurt a baseline still improving at epoch 20.
mechanism: Dropout adds training noise and reduces co-adaptation; train loss is measured in eval mode.

cfg.description: Clipping should activate at normal LR and may slow learning.

hypothesis: Clipping should activate at normal LR and may slow learning.
mechanism: Global norm threshold is half the baseline epoch-mean norm; actual clipped-step fraction is recorded.

cfg.description: Ten-fold LR may cause large gradients, unstable loss, or divergence.

hypothesis: Ten-fold LR may cause large gradients, unstable loss, or divergence.
mechanism: Stress-test reference changes LR; compare clipping only against this same high-LR run.

cfg.description: At the same high LR clipping may limit spikes, but cannot guarantee stable convergence.

hypothesis: At the same high LR clipping may limit spikes, but cannot guarantee stable convergence.
mechanism: Compared with clip-high-none only clip_norm changes; norms are logged before clipping.

cfg.description: Mixed precision may not improve end-to-end speed on this small MLP; numerical trajectories may change.

hypothesis: Mixed precision may not improve end-to-end speed on this small MLP; numerical trajectories may change.
mechanism: BF16 has an FP32-like exponent range; FP16 has narrower range and needs loss scaling. Parameters and evaluation remain FP32.

cfg.description: Zero initialization leaves hidden ReLU gradients zero; only output bias can learn class priors.

hypothesis: Zero initialization leaves hidden ReLU gradients zero; only output bias can learn class priors.
mechanism: Identical zero neurons preserve symmetry and ReLU derivative at zero is zero.

cfg.description: Small normal weights shrink activations and may delay convergence.

hypothesis: Small normal weights shrink activations and may delay convergence.
mechanism: Normal std=0.01 is independent of fan-in; repeated layers can attenuate signal.

cfg.description: Xavier may shrink ReLU activations relative to He; a shallow MLP may still train well.

hypothesis: Xavier may shrink ReLU activations relative to He; a shallow MLP may still train well.
mechanism: Xavier normal variance=2/(fan_in+fan_out); He variance=2/fan_in for ReLU.
